title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: How does stego validate give back the settings that checking filled in?
description: ST-DECL-UC07-R03-T01 and ST-DECL-UC07-FL-T expect the settings that checking reports to hold the retention 24h, or Required on, the retention 48h and the fingerprint; ST-DECL-UC05-R01-T01, UC05-R03-T01, UC05-R04-T01, UC05-FL-T and UC09-R01-T02 expect the same for tenancy, audit and modes. stego validate (ST-DECL-CLI02) prints only accepted and the faults, and the read model Faults (ST-DECL-RM01) holds only faults, so no test can read a setting that checking filled in, and these tests cannot be written as recorded. Options: (a) the JSON document of stego validate --json also holds settings: each setting of the declaration with every omitted value filled in by its default, such as idempotency with retention 24h and fingerprint body; ST-DECL-CLI02 and a read model of the settings (or new fields of ST-DECL-RM01) say so; (b) another command or flag prints the filled-in declaration, such as stego validate --settings, and the tests run it; (c) the tests prove the defaults at the unit level through a Declaring function, and the system tests check only the exit. Recommendation: (a). The flows ST-DECL-UC05-FL-S02 and ST-DECL-UC07-FL-S02 already say that STEGO accepts the declaration with the defaults it filled in, one document keeps what an agent reads in one place (ST-BO05), and the three use cases then share one form.

title: Which values of Retention and Fingerprint does checking accept?
description: The Idempotency setting (ST-DECL-EN13) says that Fingerprint is body, body+query or none and that Retention is how long a key is kept, 24h by default, but no invariant refuses another value, so checking accepts fingerprint bodyy or retention forever, and generation would meet a value it cannot use. The runtime fingerprint (ST-SUP-RP07-LC05) also covers only the method, the path and the body, so body+query and none have no runtime to call. Options: (a) add an invariant that Fingerprint is one of body, body+query and none, and Retention is a positive duration such as 24h or 48h, with a fault that names the allowed values; (b) narrow Fingerprint to body until the runtime covers the query, and refuse other values; (c) leave the values to generation to refuse. Recommendation: (a), or (b) if body+query and none are not needed yet: a fault at checking names what to change (ST-BO05). Also, the term Idempotency key (ST-DECL-TM15) says a client sends the key with a create or an update, but ST-DECL-INV25 refuses update (decision on ST-DECL-Q01); it could say a create or a patch.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.
